paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Two people in this psalm are standing in the same world, and they are trusting two very different things. The mighty man trusted "the abundance of his wealth" and strengthened himself by destruction (Psalm 52:7). David trusts "the loving devotion of God" (Psalm 52:8). And one of those foundations is going to hold, and the other one is going to get UPROOTED.

Now look at how David handles the bragger. He doesn't brag back. He says the loving devotion of God "endures all day long" (Psalm 52:1), and I think that's the whole point. When somebody's loud, powerful and wrong, it's easy to feel like THEY are the ones in charge. David says no, God's loving devotion is the thing that lasts, and the mighty man's tongue and money are not.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. Where are you putting your weight, baker? David says he is "like an olive tree flourishing in the house of God," and he praises God and waits on His name "in the presence of Your saints" (Psalm 52:8-9). Plant yourself in God's loving devotion, stay close to His people, and you'll be standing when the bragging is done.
